newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE CANOLA ENDS UP ON FUND AND COMMERCIAL DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: WCE CANOLA ENDS UP ON FUND AND COMMERCIAL DEMAND.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola ended $0.60 to $4.40 a tonne higher on fund and commercial demand, traders said.
"Funds covered about 400 November shorts, commercials bought below the market and locals turned late buyers," a trader said.
November WCE canola crush profit margin fell to -23.49 Wednesday from -20.78 Tuesday. About 800 Sep-Nov spread from $2 to $1, Nov-Jan $3. Volume was 4,025 lots.
September canola rose $4.40 to $363.20 amd November settled up $2.90 at $364.30.
November flax up $5.90 to $299.70 on local and commercial buying. Sep-Nov $12, Nov-Jan $2. Volume was 590.
"The Dec corn touched US$2.74 a few times but never went over it so hedges, commercial and local selling pushed the barley lower on the day," a feed grain trader said.
October western barley fell $2.10 to close at $135 and December fell $2.70 to close $136.50 on commercial and local selling. Volume was 1,200 lots. Feed peas did not trade.
October barley spread to October wheat at $24.30.

October feed wheat fell $0.80 to settle at $159.40, and December slipped $0.80 to close at $159.20. Activity was mostly linked to local and commission selling, traders said. Mar-May spread at $0.50. Volume was 1,289 lots.
Commercials bought 20 March oats down US$1 at US$128.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, feed peas.)
